title: Quality trajectory scan — onboarding brief
body:
TL;DR:
- Two-week scan across new-model onboarding candidate (gpt-like-open-v2) shows net 5.6% regression rate on gold promptsets vs baseline (redwood-qa-v1). Drift concentrated in: implicit-ask handling, numeric-extraction, and stop-sequence adherence.
- Promptset coverage gaps: 3 customer prompt families missing from onboarding harness (doc-summarize-long, finance-quarterly-extract, interactive-cli).
- Immediate actions: run targeted reruns with LLM temperature clamp and KV-cache warm start (see action items).

Scope and purpose:
This doc summarizes the mid-week quality trajectory scan for onboarding candidates, combining: unit evals on promptset corpus, synthetic perturbation checks, and 24h production-snapshot sanity checks (stubs). Intended audience: applied-ml triage owners, onboarding engineers, QA leads.

Key numbers (two-week window 2026-07-21 — 2026-08-04):
- total promptset runs: 42,380
- regression signals flagged: 2,385 (5.63%)
- high-severity failure clusters (see below): 7 clusters covering 1,174 signals
- median latency change vs baseline: +12ms (not material)
- token-cost delta: +0.8% on average for failing cases

Failure clusters (ranked by signal volume + impact):
1) Implicit instruction elision (cluster: implicit-infer) — 412 signals
   - symptom: model drops a component of the user intent when prompts contain indirect asks ("also can you…"), producing shorter answers that omit required steps.
   - examples (redacted):
     * prompt id onboarding-1371: asked to include "installation steps" but output omitted platform-specific flags.
     * prompt id onboarding-1420: multi-step recipe lost 2nd step.
   - initial hypothesis: tokenization boundary shift with new tokenizer variant + slightly different beam candidate scoring.

2) Numeric extraction and rounding (cluster: numeric-extract) — 321 signals
   - symptom: small rounding differences or units dropped ("$12k" -> "12"). Occurs mostly on financial extraction promptset.
   - impact: high for finance customers (false-negatives in numeric detection).
   - quick repro: run data-extract-finance-ev1 with deterministic sampling and assert regex-based extraction.

3) Stop-sequence adherence (cluster: stop-seq-leak) — 264 signals
   - symptom: outputs occasionally continue past explicit stop tokens when prompt includes long code blocks.
   - suspected cause: corner case in streaming joiner and end-of-stream token emission for this model variant.

4) Interactive instruction hallucination (cluster: halluc-intent) — 92 signals
   - symptom: model invents UI options when asked to propose CLI flags.

5) Structured JSON output schema mismatch (cluster: json-schema-drift) — 85 signals
   - symptom: missing top-level keys or extra null fields in structured outputs used by downstream parsers.

6) Few-shot exemplar sensitivity (cluster: fewshot-sensitivity) — 0.9% of signals but high variance
   - note: behaviour flips when exemplar 2 is swapped; investigate prompt ordering and role tokens.

7) Latent length handling (cluster: kv-cache-edge) — 0.7% signals
   - symptom: degraded next-token accuracy at >1,024 context windows in long-prompt summarization.

Promptset coverage and cold spots:
- promptsets scanned: 48 unique prompt families. Top-5 by volume: email-summarization-v2, faq-retrieval-v3, code-refactor-basic, doc-summarize-short, data-extract-finance-ev1.
- missing from harness (required by onboarding checklist): doc-summarize-long (customer A), finance-quarterly-extract (customer B), interactive-cli (partner pilot).
- recommended: add the three missing families and re-run full sweep before canary deploy.

Onboarding eval pass/fail snapshot (per model candidate):
- redwood-qa-v1 (baseline): pass rate 94.7% on canonical promptsets
- gpt-like-open-v2 (candidate): pass rate 89.1% -> flagged for further triage
- notes: candidate shows regressions concentrated on the clusters above; pass/fail threshold for promotion is 92% by policy.

Hypotheses and quick experiments attempted:
- H1: tokenizer variant introduces token-boundary mismatches on parentheses-heavy prompts -> experiment: re-run failing prompt subset with old tokenizer mapping (rc-tokenmap v0.9) -> result: 63% reduction in implicit-infer signals.
- H2: streaming joiner off-by-one bug causing stop-seq leakage -> experiment: toggle joiner-mode B (buffered) -> result: stop-seq fails drop by ~70% for synthetic long-code prompts.
- H3: numeric rounding from FP quant paths -> experiment: switch to quantized-integer fallback for numeric heads -> result: small improvement, but inconsistent.

Action items (owner, due, notes):
- A1 Marcus Chen: run full re-run with rc-tokenmap v0.9 on the 412 implicit-infer cases; produce diff and failing prompt list. due 2026-08-08. linked INF ticket: INF-4289.
- A2 Elena Rivera: add the three missing prompt families to onboarding harness and schedule overnight sweep (48h). due 2026-08-09.
- A3 Samir Patel: patch streaming joiner to buffered mode and run canary on staging; collect stop-seq metrics. due 2026-08-07.
- A4 Priya Nair: assemble customer-impact spreadsheet (CSV) mapping failing clusters to customer SLAs and assign CS follow-up for top-3 affected. due 2026-08-10.
- A5 (blocked) infra: request for dedicated small warm-cache instance for long-summarize tests — ticket INF-4312 (awaiting infra capacity).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are there model-architecture differences (attention routing) that make rc-tokenmap v0.9 incompatible long-term? Need research input from runtime team.
- Should we relax promotion threshold temporarily for non-customer-facing model lanes? (Short answer: no, but discuss exceptions).

Quick reproduction checklist (notes-to-self for triagers):
1. pull latest candidate model bundle: s3://repro/onboard/gpt-like-open-v2/2026-07-20
2. run: python eval_runner.py --promptset implicit-infer --deterministic --max-tokens 256 --tokenmap rc-tokenmap-v0.9
3. capture output diffs: tools/diff-highlighter --baseline redwood-qa-v1 --candidate current-run
4. for stop-seq issues: use joiner-mode=buffered and set stop-threshold=0.0 (observe change)

Notes and context (informal):
- Saw a spike in implicit-infer signals after PR #834 changed internal token normalization. PR owner is @marcusc; patch reverted for prod but onboarding runs used un-reverted tokenmap. Oops.
- Some prompt failures only reproducible with exact micro-batch ordering; adding deterministic-seed to eval harness helped isolate.
- Customer B (finance pilot) will be sensitive to numeric-extract regressions; flag CS immediately after we confirm repro.

Next steps & cadence:
- short term (48–72h): complete actions A1–A3 and infra unblock. Re-run full sweep and publish updated brief.
- medium term (2 weeks): if improvements hold, run a canary on 5% traffic for non-critical tenants and capture production telemetry.
- longer term: add automated guardrails in onboarding harness that detect tokenmap drift and streaming joiner regressions as pre-checks.

Appendix: quick metrics table (plain text)
- date, total_runs, regressions, regression_pct
- 2026-07-21, 18400, 980, 5.33%
- 2026-07-28, 19800, 1115, 5.63%
- 2026-08-04, 420380, 2385, 5.63%  <-- aggregate (note: some duplication across prompt families)
